scope: Key provisioning, owned-workspace/debug-log cleanup, and encrypted pre-M4 migration; not full M4 acceptance
checks: Key creation and matching recovery copy are private and idempotent; existing keys and mismatched copies are not overwritten. Linked/unsafe parents and a held daemon lock are rejected.

Owned operation workspaces carry a locked marker through active backup, export-download and restore lifetimes. Cleanup preserves active, foreign and unmarked directories, handles interrupted marker writes, and drains bounded batches.
Only expired debug logs matching the owned timestamp/GUID filename are removed; normal logs and locked files remain.
Cleanup runs at startup, hourly and through the administrator retention endpoint with scope and session step-up checks.

An initialized legacy schema requires a complete encrypted backup before M4 DDL. Missing keys and partial backups refuse the upgrade. Interrupted migration retries preserve user data and encrypted archives.
The pre-upgrade encrypted archive authenticates, contains the old schema and account, and can be installed with staging migration and an advanced epoch.
M4 schema state and index are recorded as version 4. Obsolete M0 plaintext rollback copies are removed only after both stores complete.
Composition and OpenAPI snapshot changes were reviewed; additive services and the operations cleanup result are expected.
limitations: No production key, archive, configuration, subscription, data, or service changed. Off-server recovery-copy custody remains an operator responsibility.
Unmarked workspaces and retained restore rollback directories are intentionally preserved. This checkpoint adds expiry for the owned debug-body filename format, not a debug-body logging producer.

Full daemon backup/restore under sustained writes, external mount-point restore, large-corpus qualification, hardened deployment, real transcript acceptance, enrichment/providers/budgets and release operations remain open.
